name: grmtools (lrpar / lrlex)
description: Yacc-compatible LR parser generator with automatic error recovery (CPCT+)

license.comment: `license = "Apache-2.0/MIT"` (dual) on lrpar, lrlex, cfgrammar and lrtable.

approach.comment: Yacc `.y` grammar and Lex `.l` lexer files compiled to Rust at build time via `CTLexerBuilder`/`CTParserBuilder` in `build.rs`; runtime generation (`RTParserBuilder`) is also possible.

implementation.comment: All four crates (lrpar, lrlex, cfgrammar, lrtable) are pure Rust with `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; dependency tree (regex, wincode, vob, packedvec, syn/quote for codegen, ...) contains no C/C++.

crates-io.comment: grmtools is a suite: `lrpar` (parser generator + runtime), `lrlex` (lexer generator), `cfgrammar` (grammar representation), `lrtable` (LR tables), `nimbleparse` (CLI). `lrpar` is the main crate; all are versioned in lockstep.

documentation.comment: The grmtools book (mdBook: quickstart, lexing, parsing, error recovery, AST evaluator, per-library chapters); API reference at docs.rs/lrpar and docs.rs/lrlex.

latest-stable-version.comment: Checked 2026-09-19; published 2026-07-22 (CHANGES.md dated 2026-07-20). Research reflects grmtools 0.15.x (edition 2024, `wincode` serialisation, `%grmtools{}` header sections introduced in 0.14.0).

grammar-class.comment: `lrtable` builds LR(1) state tables using Pager's algorithm ("A Practical General Method for Constructing LR(k) Parsers", 1977) to merge weakly-compatible states, giving LR(1) power with near-LALR table sizes. No LALR(1)-only mode.

grammar-definition.comment: Yacc-style `.y` grammar (with a leading `%grmtools{yacckind: Grmtools}` section) and Lex-style `.l` lexer file, processed by `build.rs` and included via `lrpar_mod!`/`lrlex_mod!`.

left-recursion.comment: LR(1) generator: the quickstart calculator grammar uses left-recursive `Expr: Expr '+' Term` rules. Per Assessment Guidelines LR generators get `native`.

ambiguity-handling.comment: `CTParserBuilder::error_on_conflicts` defaults to `true`: any shift/reduce or reduce/reduce conflict not resolved by `%left`/`%right`/`%nonassoc`/`%prec` (or declared via `%expect`/`%expect-rr`) fails the build with a spanned conflict diagnostic. Accept/reduce conflicts are always a hard error.

backtracking.comment: Deterministic table-driven LR parse over a `Vec<StIdx>` state stack; the only search happens inside CPCT+ error recovery, not in normal parsing.

lexer-integration.comment: `lrlex` (bundled Lex-compatible generator, regex-crate based, with start states) is the default lexer; `lrpar` is generic over the `Lexer`/`NonStreamingLexer`/`Lexeme` traits so any hand-written lexer works (`calc_manual_lex` example, `CTTokenMapBuilder` generates `T_*` token-id constants).

precedence-pratt-support.comment: Yacc `%left`, `%right`, `%nonassoc` declarations and per-production `%prec`; `lrtable` resolves shift/reduce conflicts by precedence level then associativity exactly as Yacc does.

unicode-aware.comment: lrlex compiles `.l` rules with the Rust `regex` crate over `&str` (`regex.unicode` flag, on by default in regex, togglable in `%grmtools{}`); `NonStreamingLexer::line_col()` reports columns in characters, not bytes.

input-types.comment: lrlex lexes `&'input str`. `LRNonStreamingLexer::new(input, lexemes, newlines)` accepts a pre-built lexeme `Vec`; any type implementing `NonStreamingLexer` is accepted by the parser. No `&[u8]` support.

streaming-partial-input.comment: The parser collects the whole lexeme stream up front (`lexer.iter().collect()`) before parsing; the parse API takes a `NonStreamingLexer`. A bare `Lexer` trait exists but there is no 'need more input' signal or resumable parser.

zero-copy.comment: Rule return types may use the `'input` lifetime; `$lexer.span_str(lexeme.span())` yields `&'input str` borrowed from the input.

span-tracking.comment: `cfgrammar::Span { start, end }` in byte offsets on every lexeme and via `$span` in actions; `NonStreamingLexer::line_col(span)` converts to `((line, col), (line, col))` and `span_lines_str` returns the enclosing source lines. Span type is fixed (not user-definable).

output-model.comment: `YaccKind::Grmtools`: each rule declares a Rust return type built by its action. `YaccKind::Original(GenericParseTree)` instead produces an untyped parse tree (`calc_parsetree` example).

semantic-actions.comment: Yacc-style `{ ... }` action blocks with `$1..$n`, `$lexer`, `$span`; lexeme symbols arrive as `Result<Lexeme, Lexeme>` (Err = inserted by error recovery).

whitespace-comment-handling.comment: Lex rules with an empty/`;` action discard the match (quickstart: `[\t ]+ ;`); comments are handled the same way. Parser never sees trivia.

stateful-parsing.comment: `%parse-param <name>: <Clone type>` (tuple for several) plus `%parse-generics` for type/lifetime parameters, threaded into every action; the `calc_ast_arena` example passes a `bumpalo::Bump` this way.

error-recovery.comment: CPCT+ (Diekmann & Tratt, "Don't Panic! Better, Fewer, Syntax Errors for LR Parsers") is on by default: it searches for minimal-cost insert/delete/shift repair sequences without any grammar annotation and continues parsing. `RecoveryKind::None` disables it. Tunable via `%avoid_insert`; a search timeout applies to pathological inputs (<2% of real-world cases per docs). Lexer errors are recovered by emitting faulty lexemes.

multiple-errors-per-parse.comment: `parse()` returns `(Option<T>, Vec<LexParseError>)`; the book's stated goal is letting users "fix all their syntax errors in one go".

expected-token-reporting.comment: `ParseError { stidx, lexeme, repairs }` carries ranked repair sequences (`Insert(TIdx)` names tokens that would be valid) rather than the full set of acceptable tokens at the failure state. `stidx` exposes the LR state for users who query the table themselves.

custom-error-types.comment: Parse errors are always `LexParseError<StorageT, LexerTypesT>` / `ParseError`. Only the lexer error type is pluggable (`LexerTypes::LexErrorT` implementing the `LexError` trait); user actions can return their own `Result` values but cannot inject errors into the error list.

error-span-fidelity.comment: Guideline 4: every runtime `ParseError`/`LexError` carries the offending lexeme's byte-range `Span` (line/col via the lexer); repair lexemes carry spans too. No labelled secondary spans on runtime errors — the multi-span `SpannedDiagnosticFormatter` (0.14.0) is used for build-time grammar conflict diagnostics.

diagnostic-crate-integration.comment: No bridge to ariadne/miette/codespan-reporting/annotate-snippets; grmtools ships its own `SpannedDiagnosticFormatter` for grammar errors and `ParseError::pp()` for runtime messages.

contextual-error-messages.comment: `%epp LEXEME "display"` gives tokens human-friendly names in repair messages and `%avoid_insert` tunes ranking, but there is no way to label rules/sub-parsers or attach custom messages; Yacc's `error` token and `yyerrok` are explicitly unsupported.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Batch LR parse over a fully collected lexeme vector; no edit/reuse API.

lossless-syntax-tree.comment: Whitespace/comments are discarded by lexer rules; output is a user-typed AST or an untyped parse tree without trivia.

syntax-highlighting-queries.comment: No query language or highlighting API.

used-by-lsp-ide.comment: Not used by rust-analyzer, Helix, Zed, or Neovim. The only editor-related project listed is `nimbleparse_lsp` (ratmice), an LSP for developing grmtools grammars themselves.

runtime-speed-tier.comment: epage/parse-benchmarks-rs JSON benchmark (rustc 1.94.1, grmtools v0.14.1, checked 2026-09-19): 182 ms vs 18 ms for hand-written serde_json (≈10.1×) — right on the moderate/slow boundary (>10× = slow per guideline). Benchmark is maintainer-authored (winnow) but reproducible and includes all competitors; parsers 'have not been validated'. Whole-input lexing into a Vec plus recovery bookkeeping likely contribute.

compile-time-impact.comment: parse-benchmarks-rs: 10 s debug build for the JSON parser (winnow 1 s, pest 3 s, lalrpop 12 s). `build.rs` runs the full LR(1) table construction and embeds the serialised grammar + state table (`wincode`) in the generated source; lrpar itself pulls syn/quote/prettyplease into the runtime dependency tree.

allocation-strategy.comment: Not allocation-free: all lexemes are collected into a `Vec` and the LR stack is a `Vec`. AST allocation is user-controlled; the first-party `calc_ast_arena` example threads a `bumpalo::Bump` via a parse parameter.

generated-code-size.comment: parse-benchmarks-rs reports 2,612 KiB release binary overhead for the JSON grammar — the largest in the table (lalrpop 1,523 KiB, combinators 60–175 KiB). Generated file embeds a serialised `YaccGrammar` + `StateTable` deserialised at startup (once per process since 0.14.2).

no-std-support.comment: No `#![no_std]`/`cfg_attr` in lrpar, lrlex, cfgrammar or lrtable and no `std` feature; runtime uses `std` (Vec, HashMap, regex, filetime).

msrv.comment: No `rust-version` in any Cargo.toml, no MSRV statement in README/book, and CI tests only current stable. Crates use `edition = "2024"`, which implies Rust ≥ 1.85, but that is a floor rather than a declared MSRV.

unsafe-usage.comment: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` in lrpar, lrlex, cfgrammar and lrtable. Dependencies (regex, indexmap, ...) do contain unsafe.

proc-macro-reliance.comment: Code generation happens in `build.rs`; `lrpar_mod!`/`lrlex_mod!` are `macro_rules!` include helpers. lrpar depends on syn/quote/proc-macro2 only as codegen libraries, not as a proc-macro crate.

build-rs-step.comment: Standard setup: `lrpar`/`lrlex`/`cfgrammar` in `[build-dependencies]` with `CTLexerBuilder::new().lrpar_config(...).lexer_in_src_dir(...).build()` in `build.rs`. Alternative: `RTParserBuilder` builds grammars at runtime, avoiding build.rs at the cost of runtime table construction.

dependency-count.comment: `lrpar` 0.15.0 normal non-optional deps: cactus, cfgrammar, filetime, indexmap, lrtable, num-traits, packedvec, prettyplease, proc-macro2, quote, regex, syn, unicode-width, vob, wincode (+ optional serde, + web-time on wasm32). lrpar is both generator and runtime crate, so codegen deps (syn/quote/prettyplease) are linked by the end binary too; `lrlex` adds 12 more.

wasm-compatible.comment: CI runs the test suite on `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (via wasm-bindgen) and `wasm32-wasip2`; 0.14.0 changelog notes improved WASM compatibility and `web-time` is used on wasm32 targets.

async-friendly.comment: Generated `parse()` is a synchronous free function over a `&dyn NonStreamingLexer` and returns plain `Vec<LexParseError>` (Copy-able lexemes + spans), so results are Send; parsing runs fine inside an async task. Input must be fully buffered text — no async streaming, and `Lexer::iter()` returns a non-Send `Box<dyn Iterator>`.

crates-io-downloads.comment: All-time downloads of `lrpar` as of 2026-09-19 (1.16M); `lrlex` 1.16M (they are almost always used together).

maintenance-status.comment: Checked 2026-09-19: merges on 2026-09-10 and 2026-08-26; releases 0.14.0 (2025-10), 0.14.1 (2026-01), 0.14.2 (2026-04), 0.15.0 (2026-07) — four releases in 12 months with substantive features (`%grmtools` sections, multi-span diagnostics, wincode migration).

documentation-quality.comment: Guideline 4: full book (quickstart, lexing, parsing, Yacc/Lex compatibility and extensions, error recovery, AST evaluator, start states, editions, per-crate chapters) plus docs.rs API docs (~81% coverage for lrpar) and seven in-repo examples. No cookbook or formal migration guides beyond CHANGES.md.

tutorial-book.comment: The grmtools book (mdBook) with a step-by-step calculator quickstart and an AST-evaluator walkthrough.

notable-users.value: GreptimeDB promql-parser, yk JIT (ykrt), Microsoft Demikernel network simulator
notable-users.comment: Verified via Cargo.toml (checked 2026-09-19): promql-parser depends on lrpar/lrlex/cfgrammar 0.14.2 (deps + build-deps); ykrt uses lrpar/lrlex 0.13 as build- and dev-dependencies (JIT IR parser); Demikernel's network_simulator lists lrpar/lrlex/cfgrammar 0.13.7 as build-dependencies. lib.rs lists 12 direct / 25 total dependent crates.

bus-factor.comment: softdevteam (Laurence Tratt's research group, King's College London). Commits: ltratt 1,188, ratmice 349, ptersilie 287, snim2 46; recent activity is ratmice authoring and ltratt reviewing/merging — effectively two active maintainers.
